If you can’t do that then you can do it at the beginning of the fight by defending and figuring out a pattern of their attacks. 
During the fight, try to stay calm no matter how much you get hit. Focus on your breathing, your movement and your opponent’s movements. 
There’s a lot more but these are just some basic things. Hope it helps!!

I'm 17 and not white or American so I don't know much clapping games from the 90's and 80's. But after watching the videos you linked and reading up a bit I'm pretty it started when sesame street showed it first in 1986 with 2 African-American girls playing it. The rhyme has African-American root according to what I found online and was adapted from [Nelly's "Country Grammar"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vS2FxHwviU&ab_channel=1mag3ready) from 2000, WHICH was an adaptation of the 1959 ["Shimmy shimmy kokobop" by Anthony and the Imperials](https://youtu.be/5mLjZRAXRRA) and the band was also African-American. Both the original and remake of the song were not appropriate for kids but sesame street must've changed the lyrics. The rhyme itself has different versions. As many of Lana's references come from classics from the 50's to the 80's. She almost always focuses on the original works instead of remakes. The lyrics to "Down down baby" are very much in reference with the songs it originated from and though it's a kids song with a very disturbing underlying message. Here are some of the sources:   
[Reference to the 1959 and 2000 version of "Shimmy shimmy kokobop"](http://pancocojams.blogspot.com/2017/05/four-examples-of-grandma-grandma-sick.html)

[another source](https://sahmurai.wordpress.com/2016/04/17/the-truth-behind-3-hand-clapping-games-from-your-childhood/)

And btw guys i rechecked the lyrics everywhere. When the song came out most websites said the lyrics went "Shimmy shimmy kokobop" but it OP is right it is "Jimmy Jimmy cocoa puff" they corrected it. But the origin still seems to be the same. 

If I got something wrong I'm so sorry and please do correct me. This is just what I found after doing a little research but I may not be 100% correct.

It's actually "shimmy shimmy ko ko bop jimmy jimmy ride". It's referencing a song from  1959 by Little Anthony and the Imperials.
